extracted.intended_audience: screenwriters, film industry professionals, journalists, and general readers interested in film/screenwriting
extracted.subtask_description: Explain how The Black List identifies and ranks unproduced motion-picture screenplays: who votes, what is eligible, how votes are cast and tallied, and notable outcomes/limitations. Useful for writers seeking to understand the list's selection process and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — unproduced screenplays
rubrics_metrics.description: The Black List is an annual survey of the "most-liked" motion picture screenplays not yet produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only screenplays that have not been produced as motion pictures are eligible for consideration; the list specifically tallies unproduced scripts ("most-liked motion picture screenplays not yet produced").

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent pool — development / studio and production company executives
rubrics_metrics.description: The ranking is based on a survey of studio and production company executives (development executives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents are industry professionals—development executives at studios and production companies—whose tastes and exposure determine which scripts receive 'likes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot format — each respondent names ten scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents were asked to name the ten best unproduced screenplays they read that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The original method (and implied ongoing practice) is that each participating executive submits a top-ten list of unproduced screenplays they liked that year; the list is built from these nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring metric — tally of 'likes'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Black List tallies the number of "likes" various screenplays are given by development executives, and then ranks them accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A screenplay's position on the Black List is determined by the total number of times it was named (liked) by respondents; higher counts produce higher rankings (the most-liked screenplay tops the list). Example: The Imitation Game topped the list in 2011 with 133 likes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caution — "most-liked" vs "best"
rubrics_metrics.description: The website states that these are not necessarily "the best" screenplays, but rather "the most liked", since it is based on a survey of studio and production company executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should interpret inclusion/ranking as a reflection of industry liking/popularity among the respondent pool, not an objective measure of absolute quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual timing and publication practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Black List has been published every year since 2005 on the second Friday of December.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is an annual snapshot (published on a consistent date each year), reflecting scripts that circulated/read during that eligibility window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special curated lists — e.g., the GLAAD List for LGBT-inclusive scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: GLAAD partnered with The Black List to create The GLAAD List, a curated list of the most promising unmade LGBT-inclusive scripts in Hollywood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate curated lists (partnerships) apply additional thematic or inclusion-focused criteria (here: LGBT inclusion) on top of the Black List's general survey methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome / impact metrics reported — production conversion, awards, hires, box office
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the more than 1,000 screenplays The Black List has included since 2005, at least 450 have been produced as theatrical films; produced films have grossed over $30 billion and received many Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations and wins. Writers whose scripts are listed often find they are more readily hired for other jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page uses production rate, awards nominations/wins, box-office gross, and downstream hiring as measures of the Black List's real-world impact on scripts and writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations / criticism — scripts may already be making the rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics note the list's reputation as a champion for "beloved but challenging" works has been overstated, since "these are screenplays that are already making the Hollywood rounds. And while, as a rule, they have not yet been produced, many of them are already in production."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an anti-pattern/limitation: inclusion can reflect pre-existing industry momentum rather than the list surfacing hidden work; interpret list membership with awareness of possible selection bias.
